title: Subagent lifecycle, decision attention, queue reasons, and persistence
objective: Represent each subagent identity and run independently, expose actionable attention and lineage, retain complete thread evidence, and restore the work view across sessions.
requirements: Agent identity is separate from run_id, attempt, batch, parent_run_id, and agent path.
Queued/running/blocked/needs-input/failed/completed/cancelled states expose deterministic reasons and progress.
One concurrent decision overlay never loses other pending requests; every request remains searchable evidence.
Latest run drives the row while prior run terminal state, transcript, acknowledgment, and evidence remain retained.
Session presentation metadata v2 restores activity history, focus, viewport, attention, and acknowledgment.
write_scope: agent runtime records, activity projection, decisions, and session persistence

acceptance.criterion: Resume creates a fresh run and preserves prior transcripts and terminal records.

Startup and post-start crash reconciliation, typed partial/timeout/cancel/interruption outcomes, per-run resume lineage, transcripts, tool counts, artifacts, and redacted verification references are durable.
Queue count and capacity/dependency reason are visible and persisted until execution starts.
Concurrent decisions retain independent waiters, including reverse-order requests for one agent, overlay safety, and exact prompt evidence.
Actionability order is needs-input, ready, failed/timed-out, running, completed, cancelled.
Same-sequence terminal advancement, 100,000 activity updates, stable O(N) history order, unread history, decision needs-input projection, and adaptive revision-driven write-through are retained.
Activity v2 metadata round-trips run history, details, acknowledgment, focus, and viewport.

remaining_risks: A live six-agent host/model soak and slow-terminal backpressure test remain operational validation, not a missing data-model feature.

result.summary: Subagents now have run-aware lineage, attention routing, group summaries, searchable transcripts, and restart-safe presentation state.
